reviews.body:
@pcbeingused333 thanks, the fix is correct: offset, string, datetime, duplicated and `MultiIndex` indexes, and every frequency, now match `augment_calendar_df(df.reset_index(drop=True))`, the default `RangeIndex` output is unchanged, and `NaT` handling still works. The test needs changes, see the inline comment.

Please also mention in the description the other cases this fixes: with a shuffled index, `main` silently gave rows each other's features (right row count, no NaN), and with a duplicated index or a `MultiIndex` it raised (`InvalidIndexError` / `NotImplementedError`).

review_comments.body: This only checks the row count, the index and that there's no NaN, so it can't catch misaligned values: with `index=df.index.sort_values()` it still passes, while a shuffled index gets the wrong features. That case was already silently wrong on `main`. Please parametrize over the index kinds (an offset `[10, 11, 12]`, a shuffled index such as `df.sample(frac=1, random_state=0)`, a duplicated index `[0, 0, 1]` and a string index), and compare `out[cols]` with `augment_calendar_df(df.reset_index(drop=True), freq="D")[0][cols]` row by row, keeping the check that `out.index` equals `df.index`.

comments.body:
Thanks, done: the test is now parametrized over offset, shuffled, duplicated and string indexes, compares the feature values row by row against the `reset_index(drop=True)` output, and keeps the `out.index == df.index` check. I also added the shuffled/duplicated/`MultiIndex` cases to the description.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
